Challenges

On-page SEO challenges costing you rankings

“My pages sit on page two and never break onto page one.”

Striking-distance pages need targeted work, not more content. We find the pages ranking 8–20 and optimise them first — they are your fastest wins.

“My titles rank, but nobody clicks them.”

A ranking without clicks is wasted. We rewrite titles and descriptions around intent and proof, then measure the click-through lift.

“Google keeps rewriting my title tags.”

Rewrites happen when titles, headings and content disagree. We align all three so the title you write is the title that shows.

“Competitors with thinner content outrank my detailed pages.”

Length is not the ranking factor — intent match, structure and authority are. We diagnose which signal is missing and fix that, not the word count.

“I optimised my pages and rankings actually dropped.”

Over-optimisation and cannibalisation are the usual causes. We audit what changed, consolidate competing pages and restore the signals.

“Hundreds of pages, but only a handful get any traffic.”

Most sites carry dead weight. We map every URL to a keyword and a job — optimise, consolidate or retire, page by page.

“Duplicate content everywhere, and I don’t know what Google indexes.”

We set canonical control and internal linking so one strong version of each page is the version that ranks.

“My pages load slowly and I don’t know where to start.”

Media is usually the biggest weight. We compress, resize and defer assets, then verify the Core Web Vitals improvement.

“My headings look fine to me, but Google doesn’t surface my pages.”

Structure is how crawlers understand a page. We rebuild heading hierarchy around the questions buyers actually ask.

“I refreshed old content and nothing improved.”

A refresh without intent re-mapping, internal links and freshness signals changes nothing. We refresh against data — and measure the result.

Our Process

Our on-page SEO process: what we optimise, what it delivers

1

On-page audit & opportunity scan

Every URL mapped to its keyword, intent and current performance — the gaps ranked by value.

2

Keyword research & page mapping

One primary intent per page, so pages stop competing with each other.

3

Title & meta optimisation

Keyword-led titles and click-worthy descriptions for every important page.

4

Heading & hierarchy optimisation

A structure crawlers and readers can follow — one promise per section.

5

Content optimisation & intent alignment

Existing content upgraded to answer the search better than any rival page.

6

URL & internal linking architecture

Clean URLs and deliberate internal links that route authority to money pages.

7

Image optimisation & Core Web Vitals

Media compressed and described properly, so pages load fast and rank in image results too.

8

Schema & structured data

Markup that earns rich results — reviews, FAQs and product details in the listing.

9

Mobile & page experience

The phone version audited and fixed first, because that is the version Google judges.

10

Tracking & continuous optimisation

Rankings, clicks and conversions monitored; the next round of pages queued from the data.

FAQs

FAQs on on-page SEO services

How fast can on-page changes move rankings?

Title and content updates on pages already ranking in positions 5–20 often move within a few weeks of re-crawling.

Do you rewrite our content?

Where needed. We start by upgrading what exists; full rewrites are recommended only when a page cannot match search intent as written.

What is keyword cannibalisation?

When several of your pages compete for the same keyword, splitting authority. We consolidate them so one strong page wins.

Will you work in our CMS?

Yes — WordPress, Shopify, Webflow, Magento and custom stacks, or we deliver change-ready documents for your team.

What is the difference between on-page and off-page SEO?

On-page is everything on the page itself — titles, content, structure, media and internal links. Off-page is the authority others grant you, mainly links and coverage. On-page comes first: there is no point earning links to pages that cannot convert the visit.
